title: The Shield Hero: A Side Story—The Hero of the Hammer and the Village of Tanuki
text: It had been a few days since Raphtalia went missing, and since the “God Hunt” began—ever since I’d lost the ability to properly channel the spirits’ power, causing dramatic and strange changes in my world…
“Hey, Naofumi!”
Just before noon, while I was getting ready at home to head to college during a break in our search for Raphtalia, my mom—who had been watching TV—rushed over to me, cell phone in hand.
“What is it…? I’ve got a class at college coming up, and I still need to keep looking for Raphtalia.”
I’d already explained that we hadn’t been able to track down Raphtalia, and she seemed to understand to some extent, but my mom spoke with an undeniably anxious expression.
“That kid’s school… has turned into a labyrinth! Look! Naofumi, it’s on the news, isn’t it!”

With that, my mom pointed intently at a news video on the screen. What was shown there was the high school my younger brother attends, a crowd of onlookers, and a news anchor. “Labyrinthification,” huh… Apparently, there have been reports for the past few days of a phenomenon being referred to by that underground slang term. A labyrinth is… for example, when the interior space of a building warps, creating a structure that’s larger on the inside than it appears from the outside. This has been likened to video games, which is why it’s come to be called the “labyrinthification phenomenon.” From there, mysterious creatures—which the government refers to as “dangerous, unknown wildlife,” though they’re already being called “demons” online—are running rampant. Of course, not only are there injured people, but there have even been fatalities by global standards… Neither I nor Atla have the slightest idea how this came to be. It would be one thing if I could use the power of God Hunting, but I can’t even use that properly anymore… On top of that, perhaps due to the “labyrinthification,” parts of the transportation networks in various regions have been cut off, and it seems travel by plane or ship has also become difficult.
“You’re the older brother, aren’t you! Go save him!”
“Why is it always me who has to go? You should ask the police or those guys who are all hyped up about ‘adventures.’ You’ve seen footage of people rushing right into the labyrinth, haven’t you?”

Why do I have to be the one to go save my younger brother, who excels in both academics and athletics? In a situation like that, my younger brother—who trains regularly—would be way more useful. Just because I’m the older brother, what kind of logic is it to ask me—an ordinary person living in modern-day Japan—to do this?

“What are you talking about, Naofumi! You’ve always been in high demand among our relatives! Everyone said you saved them, whether it was fishing or hunting! You often went out on your own, didn’t you!”
“Well… sure, I did go back to the countryside for long vacations sometimes…”

It’s true that my parents would call just me back to their hometown to help out. That’s why dissecting monsters in another world was a piece of cake for me. When I went back to the countryside, my parents were working and my younger brother had cram school, so we’d meet up later… On the flip side, during family trips, even though we had the money, I’d turn them down to hang out with friends instead.
“Monsters, was it? You can handle it, right?　“But that kid isn’t cut out for that kind of thing, so go help her!”

I’d been vaguely wondering—what on earth is with my family’s mysterious opinion of me? They told me the other day that even if I don’t get a job after graduating from college, I’m free to go to vocational school if I want, and that in the future I should either become a chef or take over a relative’s family business… Could it be that my relatives were planning to buy me out—or even arrange a job for me? They probably think I’ll just party all the time and fail to get a job. And yet, I’m actually held in high enough regard at my part-time job that they’ve even asked me to become a full-time employee. Does Mom have it in her head that I’m some kind of hunter who just spends his days goofing off?
“I’m busy looking for the missing Raphtalia! She’s not as fragile as you think, Mom. She’ll come back with a carefree smile on her face.”
“Oh… Naofumi, don’t say things like that. She’s your one and only little sister, isn’t she?　He’s so attached to you. You should take good care of him.”

“Attached”… He’s the guy who takes my dating sims without asking… He has a strict rule of only playing the ones I’ve already beaten—he absolutely refuses to play any that I haven’t cleared. When I made him play some terrible game just to mess with him, he kept asking me, for some reason, if I’d played it and which character I’d romanced.
“Maybe Ms. Raphtalia is at that girl’s school, right? ”
“Don’t force a connection there… Even if that’s true, what makes you so sure I’d be safe if I went?”

What kind of superhuman does Mom picture me as in her head? …I don’t know—it feels like all sorts of people in her mind are looking at me with eyes that say, “If it were me, I could do it.” I’m not that all-powerful. In fact, as soon as I stepped into the dungeon and checked my stats—which became visible once I entered—they were still typical of the Shield Hero: defense-focused with zero Attack Power. There’s no way I can go save anyone with stats like this. My little brother aside, where on earth is Raphtalia…? …Seriously, ever since they discovered the dungeon and everything—from transportation networks to everything else—has been paralyzed, what on earth has become of this world?
“Naofumi-sama!”
…And Atla’s been barging in every day, as if she’s doing laundry, while Raphtalia’s away. Wait, actually, she was showing up every day even back when Raphtalia was around.

“Oh, isn’t this Atla? Atla, have you seen the news? That girl’s school has turned into a labyrinth—it’s a real mess. I was thinking of asking Naofumi to go pick her up, but she says she can make it home on her own, so she won’t let him go.”
“If Lord Naofumi doesn’t want to go, there’s nothing to be done. I have a brother too, but if he couldn’t make it back from a dungeon of that level, I’d cut him loose, wouldn’t I?”

Mom is left speechless by Atla’s blunt reply. At the same time, the way she handles Fohl is almost enough to bring a tear to your eye… Well, I know from our time together that it also means she trusts him. Generally speaking, Atla’s sharp tongue only comes out toward people she likes—and, more importantly, people she trusts deeply. So Fohl and Raphtalia really have it rough. Or maybe this is what they call “tsundere”… Can’t she be a little more like the characters in manga or light novels?
“Atla, please don’t say things like that. After all, Raphtalia—the one Naofumi is looking for—might still be in the dungeon, right?”
Mom really does keep bringing that same old line up…
“Even if she were, it wouldn’t make a difference. Honestly, if Raphtalia is in the dungeon, I think she’d find her way back on her own.”
As always, it’s a cutthroat world. Plus, you can really see how much she trusts Raphtalia. Maybe I should try to stay this calm, too?
“Well… I am worried about Raphtalia. I don’t know what’s going on, and if the problem is so serious that she can’t come back even if she wants to, then we’ll have to go find her.”
“I see. I understand the situation now. Very well, then. Please leave it to me. I’ll send out a thought to help Raphtalia come back right away.”

"Sending out a thought"... It’s a side effect of becoming a Shield Spirit, but just hearing the words makes it sound pretty intense, doesn’t it? Atla pressed the index fingers of both hands to her temples, sending out a thought that could be picked up only by Raphtalia within a wide radius.
“I can’t pick up a reply, but I’m sure it’ll reach Ms. Raphtalia. Hehe… I bet she’s rushing over here in a panic right now.”
“I wonder what kind of thought she actually sent out…”
“Phew… If I do this, Raphtalia will come flying back. Otherwise, it wouldn’t be any fun.”
“You know, despite everything you say, you really do care about Raphtalia, don’t you…”
While we were doing that, Mom started calling out to me, begging me to go save my little brother. Sigh… I guess I have no choice but to go? Otherwise, she’ll probably keep nagging me.
“Fine, fine… I get it. I’ll go, okay? I’ll go.”
And so, I reluctantly decided to leave the house.
†(ᐢ⓿ᴥ⓿ᐢ）

Um, first, I should get a handle on the current situation. My name is Raphtalia. I had come to Lord Naofumi’s world and was living with him, but one morning… I woke up in the middle of some strange mountain I didn’t recognize. Wondering what on earth was going on, I tried to check things out by attempting to use my God-Hunting power and interact with the hammer, but as a Hero, the hammer can only be used to check stats or enhance abilities. And… this might be the biggest problem of all—for some reason, I’m now in the form of a Raph-species, like Raph-chan. To top it all off… this mountain where I woke up…
“What!? You! You say you want to leave this village and go to human settlements?!”
“Yes. I can’t stay in a place like this forever.”
“You can’t! You absolutely cannot!”

And the one yelling right in front of me right now… seems to be the village chief of the tanuki village in these mountains. He looks like an elderly tanuki with white hair mixed in his fur. He looks like a much older version of that Shigaraki-yaki pottery that Naofumi-sama showed me. I won’t say it outright, but a certain part of him is rather large. Well, I don’t really understand it, but it seems that in Naofumi-sama’s world, mysterious tanuki understand human speech and have built a civilization and are living in a village where no humans reside. That’s it, isn’t it? Is this a hidden village inhabited by beings different from humans, like the ones in the video games and manga that Naofumi-sama owns? It seems such settlements exist in my world as well, but it appears I’ve somehow stumbled into one of them. So, I thought it was a tanuki village a moment ago—and yes, the residents of this village are all tanuki. And apparently, to leave the mountains—or rather, to leave the village—I have to break through the barrier surrounding it, but it’s been set up so that one can’t just leave easily; I’ve been told I need permission from the village chief, which is why I’ve come to speak with him. However, well, as an outsider, I’ve been refused permission to leave. To begin with, did a village like this… even exist in Naofumi-sama’s world? It all seems rather suspicious.
“We have lived in hiding, far from the human settlements where dangerous people dwell, for many years. Village law strictly forbids us from ever going to human settlements!”

“Even so, I’m a complete outsider with no connection to this place, aren’t I? I have no intention of speaking about this village outside, so wouldn’t you mind letting me out? The barrier will still hold even if I leave, won’t it?”

I have a vague feeling that if Lord Naofumi knew about this village, he’d probably say he wants to come visit—but I’ll just ignore that thought. Knowing Lord Naofumi, who’s smiling as he watches Raph-chan and the others, I’m actually a little scared that if a place like this existed in this world, he might try to tempt the villagers here. The sight of countless tanuki receiving food and being brushed by Lord Naofumi when I return home… honestly, I’d rather just stick to taking care of the Raph-species in my own world.

“I don’t care if you’re an outsider or not! You… I don’t remember your name, but you’re a tanuki! For us, whose numbers are gradually dwindling due to external threats, breeding is our duty! If you’re already an adult, you must find a mate… but you—are you still just a cub?”
Apparently, by tanuki standards, I’m not yet fully mature. …Does that mean my growth has been reset? Since I’m in my Raph-species form, I can’t tell.
“You probably can’t bear children yet, but you’ll be able to soon enough. In human terms, it’s the ‘Genji Project.’”
“No, I think there’s something wrong with that.”
“In any case, I’ve already prepared a mate for you!　Even if you’re just a young Tanuki, you must seal your bond for the future right awayyyyyy! Do you understand?!”
With that, the Tanuki who called himself the village chief pointed his staff at the first Tanuki who had found me sleeping in the mountains.
“Uh, um… since it’s the village chief’s order… I’ll try to smooth things over, so for now, how about I just stay in this village for a while, like the village chief says?”
“Even if you’re an outsider, there shouldn’t be a problem as long as you form a bond with someone from the village, right? Do you understand? You—female Tanuki!”

He’s quite the loudmouth, yelling at every little thing. Somehow… a sense of unease began to well up inside me. The Tanuki who first found me seems like the more gentle type, but he doesn’t seem very assertive.
“I’ve already set my heart on someone named Naofumi-sama! Therefore, I must decline this engagement.”
Ah, Lord Naofumi… He said he’d like to be called “-san” in this world, but I just can’t help adding “-sama.” It’s a habit I want to break, but I just can’t seem to get it right.
“I see. What sort of fellow is this Naofumi, and where in this village does he live?”
“Lord Naofumi is a human and does not live in this village.”

“A human, you say!? Unacceptable! Absolutely unacceptable!　Are you defying the village’s laws?! The bond I’ve ordered you to form with this one is absolute under the village’s rules! Hey! Hurry up and drum our laws into this little Tanuki’s head!”
Oh, come on… He’s just an old Tanuki who won’t listen to reason. I wonder… I’m starting to feel like I’m beginning to understand the feelings Lord Naofumi had toward King Trash of Melromarc.
Immediately afterward—a familiar sensation washed over me.
“Hero of the Hammer, Hero of the Hammer, can you hear me?”
“…Atla-san?”
“That’s right. It’s Atla.”
It wasn’t coming from nowhere, exactly. The voice reached my mind through the hammer.
“It feels like this communication is one-way, so I’m sending you a message unilaterally.”
I tried to figure out if I could reply, interfere with the hammer, or use my God-Hunting power, but I couldn’t.
“Raphtalia, I don’t know where you are, but if you don’t come back soon—starting with this story, I’ll be taking Naofumi-sama’s spot as the main heroine.”
“Atla… Is this what you meant by sending a message…?”

Ugh… Another possibility—the one the Spear Hero made me see—flashes through my mind. I won’t let him say something like, “There are plenty of others, so I don’t need you here.” I have no intention of giving up my spot next to Naofumi-sama!
“Hey, what are you talking about, you little Tanuki?”
“Even if you do come back, please take about 11 volumes to get here.”
“Eleven volumes…? What’s with that specific number! Atla-san?”
“Hey! Teach her a lesson so she never even thinks of leaving the village again!”
“B-but…”
The Tanuki who first spotted me and the village chief are arguing about something. More importantly, there’s Atla-san’s message.
‘Or, you could go find yourself a boyfriend somewhere while you’re at it? Don’t worry. I’ll heal Naofumi’s broken heart with all my heart and soul.’
“What are you talking about?!”
“Hehehe, well then, goodbye. Ms. Raphtalia, the second heroine.”

“Ugh… her provocations are as cheap as ever… In any case, if I leave this alone, Atla-san will keep hanging around Naofumi-sama… I have to get back soon! It might end up just like when I was training!”

It reminded me of when I returned from my training in the Hengen Muso Style. That was the period when Atla sneaking into Lord Naofumi’s bed had become a constant source of worry. I have a bitter memory of how things only got worse after I asked Sister Sadeena for help. Just as I was reminiscing about that bitter memory, a Tanuki claiming to be the village chief approached me with a lewd grin and pounced.
“Guhahaha… You coward! Fine, then. If you don’t seal the bond soon, I’ll make you my eighth female—fube—!?”
Without thinking, I gripped my hammer tightly and knocked him flying.

“Gnuu! How dare you hit me! I won’t forgive this! I’ll personally make you scream in agony!　Even if you’re just a young Tanuki, my sexual desire knows no bounds! Gufufufu! I’ll teach your body a lesson myself, waaaaaah! If you have a problem with that, try defeating me! Young Tanuki—lolis are the best, ooooh! Go ahead and try to resist if you can—if you think you can, that is, aaaaaah!”
“Um, Village Chief…”
“No, that’s a bit too much, even for me.”
“I’ve been thinking this for a while, but our motto is supposed to be monogamy. Are you really a Tanuki?”
The other Tanuki dogs were recoiling from their own leader.
I heard a snap—something inside me snapped. That’s right. I remembered when the Spear Hero called me a “raccoon pig.”
“Guh! Guh-guh! Ugh! Wait—”
Driven by rage, I was giving a “lesson” to the randy Tanuki—who claimed to be the village chief—as he lunged at me.
“Gnuu! You bastard! You’ve gotten way too cocky—taste the power of my sorcery, you fooool!? W-what!? You’re telling me it’s not working?! Guh!?”

He was putting up some kind of resistance, but I decided to keep hitting him with my hammer until he apologized or surrendered. In retaliation, the Tanuki claiming to be the village chief tried biting me, swinging his fists, and using Magic, but I parried every attack and kept striking him. It was just a back-and-forth battle… but for some reason, Naofumi-sama in my memory calmly remarked, “It’s like I’m winning a no-damage victory in some retro boxing game or a battle among noblewomen.” I don’t know what the Naofumi-sama in my memory is trying to tell me. Ah… I found myself feeling a renewed sense of respect for Naofumi-sama, who had been the target of Trash-san’s grudge. After all, Naofumi-sama is someone who cannot attack others. Even though resolving problems through violence is something Naofumi-sama alone cannot do, he still managed to make his opponent pay for his actions. That’s a really tough thing to do, isn’t it? Is my use of violence just a sign of weakness…? In any case, I think Naofumi-sama was truly amazing.
“You’re getting way too cocky, aaaaaah!”
I block the swinging fist with one hand and strike back with the counter’s hammer, as if to deliver the finishing blow.
“Rough Smash Plasma!”
…I ignore the battle cry from the Naofumi in my memory.
“Aaaaaah…”
The Tanuki that spotted me first seems to have lost its nerve, but I don’t care.
“If you don’t cut it out, I’m going to play gateball with your most precious part, you know?”
I swung the hammer back with all my might and warned the Tanuki dog claiming to be the village chief, who was lying on his back. It didn’t look like he’d calm down unless I did something like this.
“Guh, I give up. What a powerful female Tanuki you are.”
“Please don’t call me a female Tanuki.”
‘Raph-chan—’
I’m not the Demon King Raph-chan either.
“If you’re that strong, then so be it… You’re the next village chief! I’ll step down. Stay here and protect everyone.”
And so, the Tanuki claiming to be the village chief—who’d just been beaten to a pulp—tried to move the conversation forward as if acknowledging my strength, but we weren’t getting anywhere.

“Were you even listening to me? I want to leave this place. Since I’ve become the village chief, I’ll use my authority to leave the village. You remaining tanuki can run the village or whatever you like. Well then, I’m off.”

At this point, I feel there’s absolutely no point in continuing this conversation. If reason doesn’t work, I’ll have no choice but to resort to force. That said, since I’ve acknowledged him as the village chief, I suppose I might as well try using that authority.
“Nooo! The village chief is trying to leave the village! Everyone, stop him! For the sake of the next generation, don’t let a strong village chief get away! Surround him and capture him!”
BoOOOOOOM! A sound like a conch shell echoed throughout the village.
“Nothing’s changed at all! I have to get back soon! Fine, I’ll just brush off whatever sparks fly my way!”
I stomped on the belly of the Tanuki claiming to be the village chief and gave him a good kick right where it hurts.
“Gugya—!? Ouch!?”
Foaming at the mouth, this noisy Tanuki finally fell silent. He was pretty tough.
“Well then, I’ll be off.”
I dashed off and sprinted toward the entrance to the village’s barrier, bursting right through it.
“Ugh… You wretched, super-powerful female Tanuki… For the prosperity of my species, I will not let you escape, no matter what… I swear.”

Beyond that… apparently, there’s something called a labyrinth that serves as a second barrier. First, I have to escape from here. Otherwise, Atla-san will end up staying by Lord Naofumi’s side forever! And the next thing I have to do is quickly return to my human form—there’s no way I can go back to Lord Naofumi looking like this.
“I have to… turn back into a human as soon as possible!”

If I were to meet Lord Naofumi looking like this, I’d… end up being treated like Filo or Raph-chan. I absolutely must prevent that at all costs… I must! In my head, I feel like Lord Naofumi might be thinking, “Isn’t this form okay?” or hoping that I’ll grow up to look like Rat-san’s “Mii-kun” or a big Raph-chan. That won’t do!
“I’ll definitely make it back to Lord Naofumi! Atla! I won’t give Lord Naofumi up!”
And so, my adventure to reunite with my Lord Naofumi began.
……Probably, there won’t be a sequel.
